newsitem.title: USA: Xerox introduces new digital printers.
newsitem.headline: Xerox introduces new digital printers.

text.p: Xerox Corp said Tuesday the next-generation of its most successful digital printing products -- DocuTech, DocuColor and DocuPrint -- will become available between now and the end of September.
It said these products are "considered critical components in the company's thrust to drive digital revenue growth and accelerate high-end market leadership."
The four products introduced today are the industry's fastest in their categories -- up to twice the speed of previous solutions, the company said.

"We have raised the productiveness quotient in three product families that already command market leadership in high-speed digital printing -- DocuTech, DocuColor and DocuPrint," said chief executive Paul A. Allaire. He delivered a keynote address at the On-Demand Digital Printing and Publishing Conference, where the products were introduced.
"They are the result of leveraging investments in technology, and linking that technology with an understanding of documents to deliver solutions that create value for our customers."

The products, being introduced into the fast-growing digital production printing arena where Xerox has more than $5 billion in revenues, underscore the company's resolve for aggressive growth in this sector.

-- DocuTech 6180 Production Publisher and DocuPrint 180 Enterprise Printing System which have laser technology that enables higher quality printing at 180 single-sheet black-and-white pages per minute -- 40 percent faster than the current industry benchmark.
-- DocuColor 70 Digital Color Production System which produces 70-high-quality full-color impressions per minute, the industry's fastest digital color production system.

-- Xerox DocuPrint 184 Highlight Color Parallel Printing System (184hc PPS) which pairs two 92 print-per-minute (ppm) highlight color laser printers driven by one print server with new Xerox "job-splitting" software for cut-sheet highlight color production speeds of up to 184 ppm.

Xeros said the DocuTech 6180 is available immediately in select cities with phased rollouts in North America, Europe, Australia and Latin America throughout 1997 and carries a base U.S. list price of $413,000.

The DocuPrint 180 will be available beginning in the third quarter of 1997 for a base U.S. list price of $490,000. The DocuColor 70 will be available beginning in September in North America and Europe with fourth quarter availability in South America for a base list price of $375,000-$390,000 (depending on digital front-end selected).
The DocuPrint 184hc PPS will be available beginning June 30 for a base U.S. list price of $490,000.
